title: Is this change ready?
lede: A decision path from a local change to review, with a visible repair loop.

nodes.label: Change ready
nodes.detail: A local change is ready for its required checks.

nodes.label: Run required checks
nodes.detail: Run the checks the repository actually defines; do not substitute invented gates.

nodes.label: All checks pass?
nodes.detail: A branch on the observed check results.

nodes.label: Ready for review
nodes.detail: The change may be reviewed. This does not imply merge or production acceptance.

nodes.label: Fix the failure
nodes.detail: Use the failing evidence to make a focused correction.

nodes.label: Rerun affected checks
nodes.detail: Rerun checks affected by the fix and other required repository checks.

edges.label: validate
edges.detail: Proceed to the defined validation commands.

edges.label: results
edges.detail: Inspect actual results, including skipped and unavailable checks.

edges.label: Yes
edges.detail: All required checks pass; hand off for review.

edges.label: No
edges.detail: At least one required check failed.

edges.label: correct
edges.detail: Make and validate the smallest correction.

edges.label: new results
edges.detail: Evaluate fresh results rather than reusing stale evidence.

steps.title: Run the required checks
steps.body: Start from a ready change and gather the repository-defined validation evidence.

steps.title: Evaluate observed results
steps.body: Check the outputs, not just whether a command was started.

steps.title: Hand off for review
steps.body: All required checks pass. Review, deployment and user acceptance remain separate stages.

steps.title: Find the failing result
steps.body: The decision follows the observed result. A failed required check takes the repair branch.

steps.title: Make a focused correction
steps.body: Use the failure to identify the cause rather than broadening the work.

steps.title: Rerun affected checks
steps.body: Gather fresh evidence after the correction.

steps.title: Evaluate again
steps.body: This loop can repeat; passing it makes the change ready for review.

assumptions: Illustrative development process; required checks depend on the repository.
“Ready for review” is not merged, deployed or accepted in production.
Flowcharts are process diagrams, not a UML diagram type. Diamonds are decisions and rounded terminals are start/end points.
evidence: Evidence: illustrative example; no application repository was supplied.
